Criterion A: Investigating:
# Criterion A: Investigating
## What it assesses
Criterion A: Investigating assesses research into art forms and artists. You investigate an art movement, genre or artwork connected to the unit's statement of inquiry, and analyse a range of artworks by artists from that context.

## How to do well
Research artists and movements with reliable sources. Analyse how they use the elements of the art form and how context shapes their work. Record your research in your process journal.

## How it is assessed
Each MYP criterion is marked from 0 to 8 using level descriptors, which describe what work looks like at each band. Command terms such as outline, explain, analyse and evaluate show the depth required. Teachers judge the best fit across the strands of the criterion.

## Key terms
Art movement: a style shared by artists in a period
Genre: a category of artwork
Process journal: a record of your research and development
Level descriptor: a description of what work looks like at each band
Command term: a word that shows the depth of answer required
Criterion B: Developing:
# Criterion B: Developing
## What it assesses
Criterion B: Developing assesses how you develop ideas and skills. You practise and develop skills in the art form; explore and develop ideas for an artistic intention; and use feedback and experimentation to refine your work.

## How to do well
Experiment with techniques and materials. Show the development of your ideas through sketches, drafts or rehearsals. Explain how your artistic intention changed and why.

## How it is assessed
Each MYP criterion is marked from 0 to 8 using level descriptors, which describe what work looks like at each band. Command terms such as outline, explain, analyse and evaluate show the depth required. Teachers judge the best fit across the strands of the criterion.

## Key terms
Artistic intention: what you aim to communicate
Experimentation: trying out techniques and materials
Skill development: improving technique through practice

Criterion C: Creating or performing:
# Criterion C: Creating or performing
## What it assesses
Criterion C: Creating or performing assesses your finished work. You create or perform an artwork that communicates your artistic intention and shows the skills you have developed.

## How to do well
Apply your skills with control. Make deliberate choices that communicate your intention to an audience. Present the work with care.

## How it is assessed
Each MYP criterion is marked from 0 to 8 using level descriptors, which describe what work looks like at each band. Command terms such as outline, explain, analyse and evaluate show the depth required. Teachers judge the best fit across the strands of the criterion.

## Key terms
Artwork: a finished piece of art
Performance: presenting art live to an audience
Audience: the people who experience the artwork

Criterion D: Evaluating:
# Criterion D: Evaluating
## What it assesses
Criterion D: Evaluating assesses reflection on your work. You appraise your own artwork or performance; reflect on your development as an artist; and consider feedback from others.

## How to do well
Judge how well your work communicated your intention, with specific examples. Identify strengths and areas to improve. Explain what you learned and how you will grow.

## How it is assessed
Each MYP criterion is marked from 0 to 8 using level descriptors, which describe what work looks like at each band. Command terms such as outline, explain, analyse and evaluate show the depth required. Teachers judge the best fit across the strands of the criterion.

## Key terms
Appraise: judge the quality of work
Reflection: thinking about your work and learning
Feedback: responses from others to your work

# Aesthetics
## The key concept
Aesthetics deals with the characteristics, creation, meaning and perception of beauty and taste. It develops the skills to analyse and appreciate the arts and the world around us. It is one of the sixteen MYP key concepts, broad ideas that connect subjects. A key concept is a big idea that frames a unit of inquiry, and each unit also uses related concepts specific to the subject.

## In Arts
Artists make choices about beauty, style and taste, and audiences judge art by aesthetic criteria. Related concepts include composition, expression and style.

## Key terms
Aesthetics: the characteristics and perception of beauty and taste
Key concept: one of sixteen broad MYP ideas that connect subjects
Related concept: a concept specific to one subject

Identities and relationships:
# Identities and relationships
## The global context
Identities and relationships is a global context in which students explore identity; beliefs and values; personal, physical, mental, social and spiritual health; human relationships including families, friends, communities and cultures; and what it means to be human.
Possible explorations include competition and cooperation, identity formation, self-esteem, status, roles and role models, and moral reasoning and ethical judgement.

## In Arts
Create self-portraits, character studies or music about who you are.

## Key terms
Identity: who a person is and how they see themselves
Well-being: the state of being healthy and content

Orientation in space and time:
# Orientation in space and time
## The global context
Orientation in space and time is a global context in which students explore personal histories; homes and journeys; turning points in humankind; discoveries, explorations and migrations of humankind; and the relationships between, and the interconnectedness of, individuals and civilizations from personal, local and global perspectives.
Possible explorations include civilizations and social histories, natural and human landscapes and resources, evolution, constraints and adaptation, and scale.

## In Arts
Study how art changed across periods, from Renaissance painting to street art.

## Key terms
Turning point: a moment when an important change happens
Migration: the movement of people from one place to another

# Scientific and technical innovation
## The global context
Scientific and technical innovation is a global context in which students explore the natural world and its laws; the interaction between people and the natural world; how humans use their understanding of scientific principles; the impact of scientific and technological advances on communities and environments; and the impact of environments on human activity.
Possible explorations include systems, models, methods, products, processes and solutions, adaptation, ingenuity and progress, and digital life and virtual environments.

## In Arts
Explore digital art, music technology and new materials.

## Key terms
Innovation: a new idea, method or product
Model: a simplified representation of something real

Globalization and sustainability:
# Globalization and sustainability
## The global context
Globalization and sustainability is a global context in which students explore the interconnectedness of human-made systems and communities; the relationship between local and global processes; how local experiences mediate the global; the opportunities and tensions provided by world-interconnectedness; and the impact of decision-making on humankind and the environment.
Possible explorations include markets, commodities and commercialization, human impact on the environment, commonality, diversity and interconnection, and consumption, conservation and natural resources.

## In Arts
Make art from recycled materials or about environmental issues.

## Key terms
Globalization: the growing interconnection of the world
Sustainability: meeting present needs without harming future generations

Fairness and development:
# Fairness and development
## The global context
Fairness and development is a global context in which students explore rights and responsibilities; the relationship between communities; sharing finite resources with other people and with other living things; access to equal opportunities; and peace and conflict resolution.
Possible explorations include democracy, politics, government and civil society, inequality, difference and inclusion, human capability and development, and justice, peace and conflict management.

## In Arts
Study protest art, political theatre and music that calls for justice.

## Key terms
Fairness: treating people justly and equally
Human rights: rights every person has because they are human
